subject: API model deprecation: staged transition cadence + exemption triage
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: API model deprecation: staged transition cadence + exemption triage

Team —

Quick sync on the v1.2 -> v2.0 model phase-out we announced last quarter. We have a subset of customers (notably Acme Corp) that need a more gradual runway and potential short-term exemptions. I want to align product, comms, and sales on the exact cadence and the criteria we’ll use for exemption approvals.

Key asks: 
- Product: confirm the hard cut date and any compatibility shim windows (token limits, param mapping) we can officially support.
- Comms: finalize a short notice to customers and an internal FAQ for CSMs; attached is a draft customer notice.
- Sales: identify any high-risk deals that should get a dedicated migration plan or an exemption form.

Attachments: migration_checklist.xlsx, customer_notice_draft.md, exemption_form.pdf

Proposal (short):
- Week 0 (today): announce public timeline and open a 30-day migration window.
- Week 4: begin automatic routing to v2.0 for new requests; fallback allowed for pinned customers via exemption.
- Week 10: hard enforcement of v2.0; legacy endpoints return 410 with migration help link.

I don’t want to block the public announcement, but we need a rapid triage workflow for exceptions. Can each of you reply with: 1) objections/constraints, 2) who should sign exemption requests, and 3) any changes to the proposed cadence.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API model deprecation: staged transition cadence + exemption triage

Thanks Rachel — important and timely. Quick responses inline: 

On Tue, Jul 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick sync on the v1.2 -> v2.0 model phase-out we announced last quarter. We have a subset of customers (notably Acme Corp) that need a more gradual runway and potential short-term exemptions. I want to align product, comms, and sales on the exact cadence and the criteria we’ll use for exemption approvals.

1) Objections/constraints: we need to be explicit about what "compatibility shim" means. For certain sequence lengths and custom tokens we may not be able to guarantee identical logits; recommend we limit the shim to: inference API signature compatibility + tokenization mapping only. No guarantees on prompt-level parity. That reduces support burden.

2) Who signs exemptions: Product + Legal must approve any exemption longer than 30 days; short-term (<=30d) exceptions can be product lead sign-off + sales notification. We should add a documented approval flow in the exemption_form.pdf; I can update that.

3) Cadence changes: the Week 10 hard enforcement is ok if we commit to a hotfix window for critical regressions during Week 10-12. Also propose an intermediate "soft migration" at Week 6 where we start telemetry-only routing to v2.0 to catch regressions early.

I'll take ownership of the migration checklist and will push a first-pass compatibility matrix to the Drive link by EOD.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Product Manager, Model Serving

A few operational points from Comms/CS: 
- Customer notice should include a short "what to expect" section (API responses, behavior changes, and timing). The attached customer_notice_draft.md is intentionally short; customers prefer clarity and sample code snippets.
- For Acme specifically: they requested a migration workshop the week before Week 4 and a 60-day exemption window if the workshop uncovers integration debt. Suggest we capture that as a conditional exemption (requires workshop completion and product sign-off).
- CSMs will need a triage rubric (low/medium/high) for exemptions; recommend we add two fields to the exemption_form: "technical debt risk" and "business impact (revenue/latency)".
